children.name: Akania americana Romero & Hickey, 1976
children.description: An extinct fossil-leaf species of Akaniaceae (order Brassicales) described by Romero & Hickey (1976) from a leaf impression in the La Huitrera Formation near Laguna del Hunco, Chubut Province, Patagonian Argentina (early Eocene, ~52-47 Ma). With A. patagonica it documents that Akaniaceae, today restricted to eastern Australia, were widespread in the Southern Hemisphere during the Paleogene.

children.name: Akania bidwillii  Mabb.
children.description: Akania is a monotypic genus in the family Akaniaceae.

children.name: Akania patagonica Gandolfo et al., 1988
children.description: An extinct fossil-leaf species of Akaniaceae (order Brassicales) named by Gandolfo, Dibbern & Romero (1988) from Paleocene-Eocene sediments of Patagonia, known from the Huitrera Formation including the Laguna del Hunco and Rio Pichileufu early-Eocene floras. The leaf fossils support a formerly broad Gondwanan distribution of the family and close Paleogene links between the South American and Australian floras.

children.name: Bretschneidera sinensis Hemsl.
children.description: Bretschneidera sinensis, the sole species in genus Bretschneidera, is a rare, 10–20 metres (33–66 ft) tall a monotypic species of tree with large inflorescences. It is found in south and east of China, Taiwan, northern Thailand and northern Vietnam.
